findings.title: Storage error path records legacy metric instead of storage metric
findings.body: In Create, when d.Storage.Create returns an error, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage). No legacy call has been made yet; this is the storage call that failed. The metric labels the failure as a legacy failure, polluting dualWriterMetrics and making alerts/dashboards for legacy health incorrect. Should be d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage). The matching success call on line 48 uses recordStorageDuration, so the error branch is clearly wrong.

findings.title: Update error path records legacy metric instead of storage metric
findings.body: In Update, when d.Storage.Update returns an error the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage). This is the same kind of mislabel as in Create: the storage call failed but a legacy metric is being recorded. Should be d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) to match the success path on line 132.

findings.title: Storage duration label uses object name instead of Kind
findings.body: On the successful storage Delete path the code calls d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage), passing the object's name as the kind label. The error branch on line 103 correctly uses options.Kind, and every other storage/legacy recording in the file uses options.Kind. This will produce mislabeled metrics (e.g. kind=foo-uid-1234 instead of kind=Playlist) and break grouping/filtering for storage duration dashboards.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection result recorded as storage metric
findings.body: In the DeleteCollection async goroutine, the legacy call's result is recorded with d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). All other legacy paths in this file (Create line 56, Delete line 113, Update line 140) use d.recordLegacyDuration. This mislabels legacy failures as storage failures and inflates storage duration histograms; should be d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy).

findings.title: Update no longer ensures legacy receives the same object as storage
findings.body: The previous Mode3.Update computed `updated` from objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old_storage), then wrapped objInfo via updateWrapper so that the legacy store received the same updated object storage did. The new implementation just passes the original objInfo to both d.Storage.Update and d.Legacy.Update. Each store will now call objInfo.UpdatedObject with its own view of `old`, so storage and legacy can compute different updated objects (e.g. when objInfo.UpdatedObject depends on `old`, when the underlying stores have diverged, or when update validation adjusts the payload). For Mode3 where legacy is meant to be a safety-net copy of storage, silently writing different payloads defeats the purpose and can corrupt the legacy store. The wrapper pattern (or equivalent) should be preserved.

findings.title: Mode3 doc comment no longer matches behavior after async change
findings.body: The comment `// Mode 3 represents writing to LegacyStorage and Storage and reading from Storage.` is now stale: this PR made the legacy write asynchronous and described in the PR description as a `safety measure` backup, but the comment says nothing about ordering or that legacy is best-effort. Update the comment (or add a package/struct-level doc) to explain that writes go to Storage synchronously and to Legacy asynchronously as a safety net, and that reads come only from Storage.

findings.title: TestMode3_Create error case never triggers an error
findings.body: In the `error when creating object in the unified store fails` case, only setupLegacyFn is provided; setupStorageFn is nil. d.Storage.Create is the first call in Mode3.Create; with no expectation set on the mock the call returns zero values (nil, nil). The function therefore does not return early, fires the legacy goroutine, and returns (nil, nil) to the test. assert.Error(t, err) then fails. To actually exercise the storage-error path this case needs a setupStorageFn that returns an error.

findings.title: TestMode3_Delete error case never triggers an error
findings.body: Same defect as TestMode3_Create: the `error when deleting an object in the unified store` case has no setupStorageFn, so d.Storage.Delete is called on an unconfigured mock and returns (nil, false, nil). dw.Delete returns no error and assert.Error(t, err) fails. Add a setupStorageFn that returns an error from Delete.

findings.title: TestMode3_DeleteCollection error case never triggers an error
findings.body: Same defect as TestMode3_Create: the `error deleting a collection in the unified store` case has no setupStorageFn, so d.Storage.DeleteCollection returns (nil, nil). dw.DeleteCollection returns no error and the wantErr assertion fails. Add a setupStorageFn that returns an error from DeleteCollection.

findings.title: Mode3 write tests never assert that legacy was also called
findings.body: Mode3's whole point is that writes go to both Storage and Legacy. None of the TestMode3_Create / Delete / Update / DeleteCollection tests assert that the legacy store's method was invoked (e.g. via ls.AssertCalled or AssertExpectations on the legacy mock). Because the legacy call is in a goroutine the tests also need to wait for it (sync.WaitGroup, channel, or a goroutine hook in the mock) before asserting, otherwise the assertions race the goroutine and become flaky. Without these assertions the tests would still pass even if the async legacy write were silently removed.
